endorsements.quote: A QMS fosters compliance to internal (e.g., institutional review board) and external (e.g., federal, and local regulatory) bodies by standardizing multi-faceted stakeholder responsibilities with its governance, allowing auditability and traceability through the appropriate evidence and documentation, maintaining an inventory of AI technologies developed and deployed, and hosting Fig.
For example, the governing body may have direct integration with existing IRB processes to ensure ethical conduct.

As risks and potential issues are anticipated for the health software ’s implementation, a risk management plan is put in place, a document articulating how safety, bias, and other anticipated risks will be identi fied and resolved.

Systematic feedback, monitoring, and corrective & preventive action (CAPA) frameworks are key to identifying and triaging issues, escalating issues to relevant accountable departments of the organization depending on their severity, performing root-cause analysis, and continuously controlling risks and improving the AI technology.
HCOs may either maintain dedicated quality teams responsible for conducting testing or employ alternative structures designed to carry out independent reviews and audits.

Moreover, establishing a change management plan and access controls can eliminate business continuity risks, providing transparency into responsible parties and outlining the risks of any given change.

unlisted_practices: Health care organizations should implement an enterprise quality management system for health AI analogous to those in regulated industries.
Health care organizations should apply a staged approach with increasing QMS rigor as AI moves toward clinical deployment, allowing flexibility during early research.
Health care organizations should maintain back-up (downtime) processes for when an AI technology must be turned off.
Health care organizations should specify training and qualification requirements for stakeholders participating in AI development teams.

screen.reason: Commentary proposing the implementation of enterprise Quality Management Systems (QMS) frameworks to govern the development and deployment of health AI.
